reason: The cited evidence supports the baseline properties of HfMoTaTiZr (E2) and the general concept of adding low-density elements like Al to reduce density (E1), but it provides no direct support for Al substitution in this alloy system or for the specific claim that Nb addition reduces brittle intermetallics and maintains ductility; E3 actually suggests Nb decreases room-temperature strength slightly, which contradicts the premise that it sustains strength.
premises: Al substitution reduces density via atomic mass reduction while retaining solid-solution strengthening
Increased Nb content sustains ductility and toughness by reducing brittle intermetallic formation
The balance of Al and Nb maintains dislocation motion mechanisms for high yield strength at room and elevated temperatures
HfMoTaTiZr baseline has density ~10.21 g/cm³, room-temperature yield strength ~1600 MPa, and 1000°C yield strength ~855 MPa
Nb addition increases elevated-temperature strength and ductility in related RHEA systems
